passages.note: Bill overview showing Finchem as prime sponsor of SB1057 (2026), which the Governor vetoed.

passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding any other statute, any vendor that provides fraud countermeasures that are contained in and on the paper used for ballots shall be ISO 27001 certified, ISO 17025 certified or ISO 9001:2015 certified.
passages.note: The operative new section 16-504 regulates security features of the ballot paper and its vendor, not how a voter's identity or eligibility is verified.
Senate Third Reading vote page naming Finchem as a Y vote; 11 of 27 voting members voted N, so it is not near-unanimous.

rows.reasoning: Finchem prime-sponsored and voted Y on SB 1057 (2026), but its operative section requires that "any vendor that provides fraud countermeasures that are contained in and on the paper used for ballots shall be ISO 27001 certified, ISO 17025 certified or ISO 9001:2015 certified" and lists watermarks, holograms and security inks. That is ballot-stock anti-counterfeiting, not the dimension these rungs separate, which runs from "Require no identification to vote, verifying voters by signature or existing records." to "Require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote." No passage here speaks to what identification the government should require, so none survives relevance.
